integrity: The two exact identities are independently proved from the slice-infimum definitions. The Daugavet lower bound uses a scalar Hölder norming pair, the Daugavet-point property and a reverse-triangle inequality; matching upper bound comes from slices concentrating at scalar 1. The Delta lower bound preserves arbitrary containing slices by varying only the Daugavet fiber; the upper bound uses monotonicity of the exact scalar envelope. Boundary cases and strictness are treated explicitly. The bundled finite checker is supplementary; no independent audit or independent validation was performed.
scientific_limitations: Real scalar summand and 1<p<infinity only. The formula applies at unit points whose normalized second component is a Daugavet point; the complete unit-sphere and qualitative locus conclusions require the second summand to have the Daugavet property. No formula is claimed for arbitrary non-Daugavet directions, multiple scalar atoms, or the endpoints p=1 and p=infinity.
title: Exact pointwise Daugavet–Delta profile in scalar–Daugavet \(\ell_p\)-sums
